clue.text: Wide hat not something trivial

blocks.note: W is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for a wide
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A wide-brimmed hat that turns out to be nothing important.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue's words are nearly the answer already: only 'Wide' needs shrinking to its abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A whatnot is an unnamed trifling item, a small object of no real consequence.

clue.text: Dr White twisted and twisted

indicators.note: the first 'twisted' says the preceding letters are wrung into a different order

blocks.note: the doctor's title and surname used as raw letters

explanation.surface: A doctor called White who turned and turned again.
explanation.walkthrough: The same word does two jobs: once to shuffle the letters, once as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Writhed means squirmed or contorted the body, which is a past-tense synonym of the verb meaning wrenched about.

clue.text: Interesting sailor to sing going round world

indicators.note: going round means one word encircles another, wrapping around it

blocks.note: AB, able seaman, is the usual crossword sailor
taken as written
an orb is a globe, so the world

explanation.surface: A sailor bursting into song as the ship circles the globe makes for a fascinating story.
explanation.walkthrough: The sailor stands first, and the word for singing is split open to take the world inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something absorbing holds the attention completely, a close synonym of engrossing or gripping.

clue.text: She has an aunt -- English, residing in Nice

indicators.note: residing in means one item lives inside another, placed within its walls

blocks.note: the French Riviera city, taken as its letters
E is the standard abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: An Englishwoman living in Nice who has an aunt.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description rather than a synonym: every girl with an aunt is that aunt's sibling's daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece is the daughter of a sibling, so she necessarily has an aunt or uncle in the family.

clue.text: Stop and meet train when moving

indicators.note: moving shifts the letters out of their places into a fresh order

blocks.note: both words supply letters

explanation.surface: An instruction to halt and greet a train as it pulls in.
explanation.walkthrough: Trains really do terminate, so the station picture hides that the two words are only raw letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To terminate is to bring to an end or cease, a plain verb synonym for halting.

clue.text: Out of bed, taking charges to a higher place

blocks.note: someone out of bed is up
wards are people in someone's charge

explanation.surface: A guardian getting up and taking the children in their care upstairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Upwards is an adverb meaning towards a more elevated position, which matches the phrase about going higher.

clue.text: Upper-class wriggling nude is not necessary

indicators.note: wriggling suggests restless squirming, so the letters that follow shift position

blocks.note: U is the old label for upper-class usage
letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A posh person squirming about naked is quite uncalled for.
explanation.definitionFit: Undue means excessive or unwarranted, more than is called for, so not needed.

clue.text: Negative girl joins WI for claret, maybe

definitions.note: a descriptive definition: the thing used for claret

blocks.note: the Women's Institute, a British countrywomen's association, taken as written
NEG is the short form of negative
lass is a common word for a girl

explanation.surface: A gloomy young woman signs up with the Women's Institute for a drink of red wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' marks claret as just one example of what the vessel holds.
explanation.definitionFit: A wineglass is the stemmed drinking vessel used to serve red Bordeaux and other vintages.

clue.text: Praise not started, so collect is read

indicators.note: a word that has not started is missing its opening letter

blocks.note: taken as written before losing its head

explanation.surface: Applause that never began, so the church collection is read out instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collect is read' tells the solver how to take 'collect': as the definition, in its fundraising sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise money is to gather funds, the same sense as collecting for a cause.

clue.text: Name of fish, not applicable in Leeds when written up

indicators.note: in places one item inside the letters of the city that follows
in a down clue, writing upwards means reading the letters from bottom to top

blocks.note: the Yorkshire city, taken as its letters
N/A is the form-filling abbreviation for not applicable

explanation.surface: A form-filler in Leeds writing 'not applicable' where a fish's name is asked.
explanation.walkthrough: The insertion goes between the last two letters of the city, and only then is the whole thing turned upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: A sand eel is a small slender sea creature that burrows in sand, a species of fish.

clue.text: Children matter

blocks.note: first meaning: offspring, as in dying without heirs
second meaning: a topic or point under discussion

explanation.surface: Children count; their welfare matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'matter' reads as a verb in the surface but is a noun in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means legal offspring and also a subject of debate, both standard dictionary senses.

clue.text: Sea-going flag to leave outside sanctuary

indicators.note: outside means the first word sits around the second, enclosing it

blocks.note: to resign is to leave a job
a den is a private retreat or refuge

explanation.surface: A sailor hauling down the flag to quit the shelter of a harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: The insertion splits the quitting word after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Red Ensign is the British merchant navy's flag, flown by civilian ships at sea.

clue.text: Thick skin manufactured from his and her doe

indicators.note: something manufactured is made by working raw materials into a new form

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Matching his-and-hers leather goods made from deer hide.
explanation.walkthrough: The skin of a doe is a red herring: the hide comes from a different animal entirely.
explanation.definitionFit: Horsehide is the tough leather from a horse, a hide notably heavier than most.

clue.text: Refugees evacuated, including some silly people

indicators.note: including some means part of the preceding words is held within them

blocks.note: the run of letters straddles the two words

explanation.surface: An evacuation of refugees, some of them foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evacuated' looks like an instruction to empty a word, but it is only there to supply letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone a goose is an old insult for a fool, so the plural means foolish folk.

clue.text: Doctor has one afterthought for weak people

blocks.note: DR is the abbreviated title
I is the Roman numeral one
a postscript is an afterthought added to a letter

explanation.surface: A doctor adds a note at the bottom of a letter about feeble patients.
explanation.definitionFit: Drip is informal slang for a dull, spineless person lacking character.

clue.text: Giant sure to scramble means of identification

indicators.note: scrambling jumbles things up, as with eggs, so the letters are mixed

blocks.note: both words supply letters

explanation.surface: A huge figure confidently scrambling an ID.
explanation.definitionFit: A handwritten name on a document is how a person proves who they are.

clue.text: Heavenly being, one with right to shift to left

blocks.note: a, the indefinite article, means one
R is the usual abbreviation for right
to shift is to change
L is the usual abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A political figure on the right moving across to the left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right to shift to left' sounds like a political conversion; it is simply four abbreviations and a verb in a row.
explanation.definitionFit: An archangel is an angel of the highest rank, such as Gabriel or Michael, a celestial spirit.

clue.text: Substance of book leads to editor being happy

blocks.note: a book's content is what it contains
ED is the standard abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: A book's material pleases its editor.
explanation.definitionFit: Contented means satisfied and at ease, a mild near-synonym of glad.

clue.text: Fighter delighted one on a rocky peak

blocks.note: glad means pleased
I is the Roman numeral one
taken as written
a tor is a rocky hilltop, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A combatant thrilled to stand on top of a crag.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means placed above, so the happy word and the numeral sit over the hilltop.
explanation.definitionFit: A gladiator was a Roman combatant who battled in the arena for public entertainment.

clue.text: Wise man not ready to see the colour of aromatic leaves

blocks.note: a sage is a wise person
unripe fruit is green, not ready to eat

explanation.surface: An unprepared wise man is shown a herb garden.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a little riddle: the herb shares its name with the wise man.
explanation.definitionFit: Sage-green is the soft grey-green shade of the culinary herb's foliage.

clue.text: Everyone in TV programme is superficial

indicators.note: in puts the first word inside the one that follows

blocks.note: a show is a broadcast programme
everyone is all

explanation.surface: A complaint that everybody on television lacks depth.
explanation.definitionFit: Shallow describes a person lacking depth of thought or feeling, the same sense as superficial.

clue.text: Scarface loses high card in this muffler

indicators.note: loses means part of the film title is taken away

blocks.note: the gangster film title, taken as its letters
the ace is the top card in many games

explanation.surface: The gangster Scarface, minus his trump card, is wrapped up in a winter neck-warmer.
explanation.definitionFit: A muffler is an old word for a warm cloth wound round the neck.

clue.text: Liberty to be fed more fudge

indicators.note: to fudge is to fiddle or fake something, so the letters are doctored

blocks.note: both words supply letters

explanation.surface: The right to be given extra helpings of a sweet treat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fudge' reads as the sweet being eaten, but it is a verb meaning to fiddle.
explanation.definitionFit: Freedom and liberty are direct synonyms for the state of not being constrained.

clue.text: Carol endlessly clinging to mother's bouquet

indicators.note: without ends means both the first and last letters are cut away

blocks.note: the girl's name with its outer letters removed
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: Carol hugs her mother and breathes in the scent of her flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bouquet' suggests flowers, but here it means a wine's smell.
explanation.definitionFit: Bouquet is the term for the fragrance of wine, so it is a synonym for scent.

clue.text: Welsh girl is partly a damfool wench

indicators.note: partly means only a portion of the following words is used

blocks.note: the letters run across the gap between the last two words

explanation.surface: A girl from Wales dismissed as a silly young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Olwen is a traditional female name from Wales, borne by a heroine of the Mabinogion legends.

clue.text: Low level of subsistence makes bride lean!

indicators.note: makes says the following letters are made into something new

blocks.note: both words supply letters

explanation.surface: Poverty leaves a newly married woman thin.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark flags that the whole sentence is also true: poverty would make anyone thin.
explanation.definitionFit: Living on the breadline means having barely enough income to survive, the poorest tolerable standard.

clue.text: Bay gee-gee taken in when loose

indicators.note: taken in means one thing is absorbed inside another

blocks.note: taken as written
gee-gee is nursery talk for a horse, shortened to its two initials

explanation.surface: A bay horse is brought into the stable after running free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bay' looks like a horse's colour, matching the gee-gee, but is just a word to be opened up.
explanation.definitionFit: Baggy clothes hang slackly and are not tight-fitting, so the adjective means slack.

clue.text: Show how DA makes enclosure for male sheep

indicators.note: an enclosure surrounds something, so the first letters wrap around the next item

blocks.note: taken as written
a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: A demonstration of how a district attorney builds a pen for a ram.
explanation.definitionFit: A drama is a play or theatrical production, which is one sense of a stage show.

clue.text: Cheap but vulgar manner to move time

blocks.note: low behaviour is coarse and common
to budge is to shift slightly
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: An inexpensive yet tasteless way of shifting the clock.
explanation.definitionFit: Low-budget describes something made with little money, so it is inexpensive.

clue.text: Behaved like Bill and Ted

blocks.note: a bill passed by Parliament becomes an Act
Ted and Ed are both short for Edward

explanation.surface: Someone who carried on like the two dim heroes of the film Bill and Ted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name to pair with Ted; it is the parliamentary sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To act is to conduct oneself in a certain way, so the past tense matches conducted oneself.

clue.text: Cheerless time to enter a grape factory?

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so one item is placed within another

blocks.note: a winery is where grapes are made into wine
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A visit to a vineyard's works in bleak weather.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark signals that 'grape factory' is a playful description rather than a standard term.
explanation.definitionFit: Wintery weather is cold and bleak, so by extension the word means dreary and comfortless.

clue.text: I'm a drag looking silly in this sketch

indicators.note: silly suggests a muddled state, so the letters appear in a jumbled order

blocks.note: the apostrophe is ignored and every letter used

explanation.surface: A bore complaining that the cartoon makes them look foolish.
explanation.definitionFit: A diagram is a simple drawing showing how something works, so a rough outline drawing.
